open_points.subject: content_identity idempotency_key variant
open_points.text: - content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the idempotency_key variant MUST build one JSON object with one member per entry of fields, named by the entry's port and holding the JSON value its canonical_json encodes, so the order of the fields does not change the key, and return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of its canonical bytes; a field whose value is null is kept as null, not dropped.
open_points.other_text: - canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
open_points.question: KeyFieldsContent permits multiple fields entries with the same port, but preserving one object member per entry would repeat that member name and canonical_bytes must reject it; must fields be constrained to unique ports, or must duplicate-port handling replace one of these requirements?
